# Vitamin B12 Monitoring and Supplementation in Metformin-Treated Patients
**All patients on metformin should have baseline vitamin B12 levels checked, followed by annual monitoring after 4 years of therapy, with immediate supplementation for confirmed deficiency while continuing metformin.** 1 , 2
Section: Vitamin B12 Monitoring and Supplementation in Metformin-Treated Patients > Monitoring Frequency > Standard Monitoring Protocol
* **Baseline assessment:** Check vitamin B12 levels before starting metformin or at first opportunity 1
* **Routine monitoring:** Begin annual vitamin B12 screening after 4 years of continuous metformin therapy, as hepatic B12 stores become depleted at 4-5 years 1 , 3
* **Hematologic parameters:** Measure hemoglobin, hematocrit, and mean corpuscular volume (MCV) annually 4

# 131-LB: Prevalence of Vitamin B12–Monitoring among Patients Receiving Metformin in a Public Hospital _Free_
Background: Metformin reduces intestinal absorption of Vitamin B12 in up to 30% of patients and lowers serum Vitamin B12 concentrations in 5-10%. In 2017, the American Diabetes Association (ADA) updated its guidelines to recommend patients taking metformin undergo regular monitoring of Vitamin B12 levels.
To better understand acceptance and application of these guidelines, we undertook an assessment of such monitoring within a single hospital center serving the low-income population in Atlanta, GA to assist in guiding optimal monitoring and patient management.

...

The prevalence of Vitamin B12 levels ordered and measured was 7.5% (674 of 8,975) among patients seen in primary care clinics and 2.3% among those followed in endocrinology (25 of 1,081) (chi-square p<0.0001) . 621 (6.9%) of the metformin-treated primary care patients had neuropathy, and of those 63 had Vitamin B12 levels.

...

Conclusion: Among two outpatient cohorts who were prescribed metformin, there was suboptimal adherence to the ADA’s recommendation for regular monitoring of Vitamin B12 levels. Approaches for increasing and optimizing ordering and monitoring Vitamin B12 levels will be developed.
Increased awareness of the relationship between metformin and Vitamin B12 deficiency and standardized approaches to monitoring are needed.

excerpts: Metformin-Induced Vitamin B12 Deficiency Presenting as a Peripheral Neuropathy DavidS.H.Bell Authors and Affiliations Southern Medical Journal [103(3):p 265-267, March 2010.](https://www.ovid.com/jnls/smajournalonline/toc/2010/03000) | DOI: 10\.1097/SMJ.0b013e3181ce0e4d Abstract In Brief Abstract: Chronic metformin use results in vitamin B12 deficiency in 30% of patients. Exhaustion of vitamin B12 stores usually occurs after twelve to fifteen years of absolute vitamin B12 deficiency. Metformin has been available in the United States for approximately fifteen years. Vitamin B12 deficiency, which may present without anemia and as a peripheral neuropathy, is often misdiagnosed as diabetic neuropathy, although the clinical findings are usually different. Failure to diagnose the cause of the neuropathy will result in progression of central and/or peripheral neuronal damage which can be arrested but not reversed with vitamin B12 replacement. To my knowledge, this is the first report of metformin-induced vitamin B12 deficiency causing neuropathy. # Metformin and B12 Deficiency
**Patients on metformin, especially those taking ≥1500 mg daily or using it long-term (>5 years), should have vitamin B12 levels measured at baseline, then every 2-3 years, with more frequent monitoring in high-risk patients, and deficiency should be treated with supplementation to prevent irreversible neurologic complications including peripheral neuropathy and autonomic dysfunction.**

## Monitoring Strategy
The 2024 NICE guideline recommends measuring hematologic parameters annually and **vitamin B12 at 2-3 year intervals** in patients on metformin 7 . The FDA label echoes this recommendation 3 .

* **Annual monitoring** for patients on ≥1500 mg daily, duration >5 years, age ≥65, or with other risk factors
